Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'set_posture' moves the hinge of an iPhone Duo (a simulator with a small outer screen and a large inner one) to 'state': 'closed' lights the outer screen, 'open' (flat) the inner one, and 'half_open' opens it to 'angle' degrees, where iOS picks the lit screen; the result says which. Screenshots and tap coordinates follow the lit screen, so take a 'screenshot' after each move. 'posture' reports the state, the hinge angle and the lit screen. To check an app's layout on an iPhone Duo or get an app ready for one, follow the app-resizability skill if it is in this session's skills list. Only skills listed in this session count, so do not search the disk for it. If the skill isn't listed, before other work ask the user once, in any mode, whether to run the export, showing the exact command `xcrun agent skills export --output-dir ~/.claude/skills` just before the question in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!" (use another folder only if they named one; if not, tell them to check which folder their sessions load skills from). Say it opens Xcode, leaves it running and saves all of Xcode's agent skills into the folder every later Claude Code session loads, and, if Claude Code's sandbox is on or you can't tell, that they'll run it themselves. Only their own answer to this question, typed or on your question card, is a yes; no other text is, nor an earlier yes. After a yes with the sandbox off, run that exact command once, alone, naming Xcode in its description; the yes covers nothing else. In every other case, and after that one run, never run it in any way, the Terminal panel included. After a no, go on without the skill. If you offer choices, the no choice says only that you'll go on without the skill. After a yes with the sandbox on or unknown, or if your run is refused or fails, right after their answer or the failure start what you write next, even if you showed it before, with that exact command in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!"; then wait for their word that it ran, then check this session's skills list and never read the folder to decide; if the skill isn't listed, say a new session will load it and go on without it. Only when the user asked to check or fix the layout on a Duo, not to review or read code: note the state and angle with 'posture'; for closed, half_open and open, call 'set_posture' and take a 'screenshot'; if the open screen shows the app with black bars and the target sets UIRequiresFullScreen, tell the user the key is the likely cause and keep it unless they ask; if the user agrees to a fix, make only that fix, then rebuild, 'launch' the app and check again; last, put the hinge back. 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag: left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator this session already uses, else a booted one no other session is using, else the first booted one. If none is booted, 'attach' boots the only one the user already allowed, and 'launch' does so or asks for 'attach' first; if there is not exactly one, name one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Search results are mixed, and the official Alibaba pricing page snippet didn't show the Qwen-VL image-input rates, so verify against the live page before relying on any figure.

- **Qwen3 VL 32B Thinking:** Aggregator LiteLLM lists $0.16 per million input tokens and $2.87 per million output tokens on Model Studio, dated November 2026 ([models.litellm.ai](https://models.litellm.ai/models/qwen3-vl-32b-thinking)).
- **Qwen3 VL 235B A22B:** LiteLLM lists $0.40 input and $1.60 output for Instruct, and $0.40 input and $4.00 output for Thinking ([models.litellm.ai](https://models.litellm.ai/providers/dashscope)).
- **Qwen3-VL Plus:** One pricing guide lists $0.20 input and $1.60 output per million tokens ([developer.puter.com](https://developer.puter.com/tutorials/qwen-api-pricing/)). FutureAGI lists no price for it ([futureagi.com](https://futureagi.com/llm-cost-calculator/dashscope/)).
- **Qwen3-VL embedding:** The official Alibaba Cloud page lists image/video input at $0.258 per million tokens, with text at a lower rate ([alibabacloud.com](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/model-pricing)).
- **Newer flagships:** A third-party guide says the Qwen3.8-Max flagship text model accepts image input directly, so a dedicated VL model is only worth using when its cheaper tier matters ([morphllm.com](https://www.morphllm.com/qwen-api)). Another guide says Qwen3.8 Omni Flash bills text, image, audio, and video input at a single $0.15 per million rate ([developer.puter.com](https://developer.puter.com/tutorials/qwen-api-pricing/)).

Sources disagree on some figures (for example, Qwen3 VL 32B Instruct is $0.16 input on LiteLLM but $0.10 on llmcostcalc), and the aggregator pages may lag or differ from Alibaba's own rates. The official Alibaba Cloud page (alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/model-pricing) is the authoritative source for the current Qwen-VL image-input rates, and the Singapore and China regions bill differently.

Search results are mixed, and the official Alibaba pricing page snippet didn't show the Qwen-VL image-input rates, so verify against the live page before relying on any figure.

- **Qwen3 VL 32B Thinking:** Aggregator LiteLLM lists $0.16 per million input tokens and $2.87 per million output tokens on Model Studio, dated November 2026 ([models.litellm.ai](https://models.litellm.ai/models/qwen3-vl-32b-thinking)).
- **Qwen3 VL 235B A22B:** LiteLLM lists $0.40 input and $1.60 output for Instruct, and $0.40 input and $4.00 output for Thinking ([models.litellm.ai](https://models.litellm.ai/providers/dashscope)).
- **Qwen3-VL Plus:** One pricing guide lists $0.20 input and $1.60 output per million tokens ([developer.puter.com](https://developer.puter.com/tutorials/qwen-api-pricing/)). FutureAGI lists no price for it ([futureagi.com](https://futureagi.com/llm-cost-calculator/dashscope/)).
- **Qwen3-VL embedding:** The official Alibaba Cloud page lists image/video input at $0.258 per million tokens, with text at a lower rate ([alibabacloud.com](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/model-pricing)).
- **Newer flagships:** A third-party guide says the Qwen3.8-Max flagship text model accepts image input directly, so a dedicated VL model is only worth using when its cheaper tier matters ([morphllm.com](https://www.morphllm.com/qwen-api)). Another guide says Qwen3.8 Omni Flash bills text, image, audio, and video input at a single $0.15 per million rate ([developer.puter.com](https://developer.puter.com/tutorials/qwen-api-pricing/)).

Sources disagree on some figures (for example, Qwen3 VL 32B Instruct is $0.16 input on LiteLLM but $0.10 on llmcostcalc), and the aggregator pages may lag or differ from Alibaba's own rates. The official Alibaba Cloud page (alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/model-pricing) is the authoritative source for the current Qwen-VL image-input rates, and the Singapore and China regions bill differently.

content.text:
结论先说：**千问现在最便宜、又能直接用在我们识别上的是 `qwen3.7-flash`。** 如果只看「读字」，`qwen-vl-ocr` 也一样便宜。两个都还没在我们的图纸上试过。

## 先说现状

我们已经接了千问，走的是 OpenAI 兼容接口（`dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1`），看 [AIService.swift:34](BeadInventory/Managers/AIService.swift:34)。换模型不用改代码，在 [docs/models.json](docs/models.json) 里加个名字就行。

官方文档写明千问的 Plus、Max、Flash 都支持图片输入。所以通用模型直接就能识别图纸，不一定要用专门的 VL 模型。

## 能识图的模型（北京区原价，元 / 百万 Token）

识别一次大约要 3000 多个输入 Token，其中图片约 2500 个，提示词几百个。输出是一段 JSON，几百个 Token。下面「一张图大概多少钱」就是按这个估的。

| 模型 | 输入 | 输出 | 一张图大概多少钱 | 免费额度 | 在不在我们清单里 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **qwen3.7-flash** | 0.2 | 0.8 | 约 0.1 分 | 100 万 Token | 不在 |
| **qwen-vl-ocr** | 0.3 | 0.5 | 约 0.1 分 | 100 万 Token | 不在 |
| qwen3.8-flash（现在的默认） | 0.8 | 2.7 | 约 0.4 分 | 100 万 Token | 在 |
| qwen3.7-plus | 2（限时打八折） | 8（限时打八折） | 约 0.9 分 | 100 万 Token | 在 |
| qwen3-vl-plus | 1 | 10 | 约 0.9 分 | 100 万 Token | 在 |
| qwen3.6-flash | 1.2 | 7.2 | 约 0.7 分 | 无 | 在 |
| qwen3.8-max | 12 | 36 | 约 6 分 | 100 万 Token | 在 |

换成用户能感受到的说法：用 qwen3.7-flash，一块钱大约能扫一千张图。100 万的免费额度大约够扫三百张。

## 我的看法

- **qwen3.7-flash 最值得试。** 它是通用模型，按格式输出 JSON 应该没问题，价格只有现在默认模型的四分之一左右。
- **qwen-vl-ocr 是专门读字的。** 我们要做的事其实就是从图纸图例里读出色号和数量，跟它对口。风险在于 OCR 模型不一定老老实实只输出 `{"items":[...]}`，要试过才知道。
- **qwen3.6-flash 可以考虑从清单里拿掉。** 它比 3.8-flash 贵，北京区也没有免费额度，留着没什么理由。
- 有个坑要留意：这些新模型都支持思考模式，思考产生的内容按输出价算钱。我们现在的请求没传 `enable_thinking`。如果某个模型默认开了思考，实际花费会比上表高不少，识别也会更慢。试的时候顺手看一下返回里的 token 用量就知道了。

## 没查到的

- 网上有文章提到 `qwen3-vl-flash`，但官方模型列表和价格页上都没有它，我就没列进来。
- 图片 Token 的算法（32×32 像素算 1 个，默认每张图最多约 2560 个）来自官方视觉文档，不过这一段我是从摘要里拿到的，不是原文。
- 表里都是原价。控制台里可能还有别的优惠，以控制台为准。

Sources:
- [阿里云百炼 模型调用价格（官方）](https://docs.bailian.console.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/model-pricing)
- [阿里云帮助中心 模型价格](https://help.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/model-pricing)
- [文本生成模型列表（含图像输入说明）](https://help.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/text-generation-model)
- [视觉理解文档](https://help.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/vision)
- [Qwen-Omni 文档](https://help.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/qwen-omni)
- [Alibaba Cloud Model Studio Pricing（英文）](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/model-pricing)
- [LiteLLM DashScope 价格汇总](https://models.litellm.ai/providers/dashscope)
- [Puter Qwen API 价格](https://developer.puter.com/tutorials/qwen-api-pricing/)

# 发布 App 内公告

App 启动时会静默拉取 `https://lwshanbd.github.io/BeadInventory/announcement.json`，通过格式校验后弹窗展示。本文档说明如何发布一条新公告。

## 发布流程

1. 在仓库根目录运行脚本生成 JSON：

   ```bash
   python3 tools/generate_announcement.py \
     --id "2026-05-01-v1.9" \
     --title "v1.9 已发布" \
     --message "新增了批量导入、修复了若干 bug。请到 App Store 更新。" \
     --output docs/announcement.json
   ```

2. 提交并推送：

   ```bash
   git add docs/announcement.json
   git commit -m "docs: 发布公告 2026-05-01-v1.9"
   git push
   ```

3. 等待 GitHub Pages 构建完成（通常 1–2 分钟），访问 URL 确认：

   ```
   https://lwshanbd.github.io/BeadInventory/announcement.json
   ```

## 重要约束

- **`id` 字段必须每次不同**。App 会记录已展示过的公告 id，重复 id 不会再弹窗。推荐格式：`YYYY-MM-DD-描述`。
- **时间戳（`ts`）必须在 `[now - 90 天, now + 1 小时]` 之间**。脚本会自动填当前时间戳，但如果公告写好了很久没发，需要重新跑脚本刷新。上界是为了容忍客户端时钟小偏差。

## 关于安全

当前实现**不做签名校验**。App 无条件信任从 GitHub Pages 拉到的 JSON。理由：

- 该仓库公开，任何签名密钥都无法真正保密
- iOS 强制 HTTPS 传输，已挡住绝大多数中间人攻击
- 公告 UI 只展示纯文本 + 一个"我知道了"按钮，没有可点击链接，攻击面非常有限
- 对一个非关键的公告系统，简单可靠胜过无效的复杂

如果未来 App 用途发生变化（例如处理支付、医疗数据等），重新评估是否需要引入签名机制。
# 更新在线模型清单

App 每次启动、每次回到前台（包括收起控制中心、通知之后），都会静默拉取 `https://lwshanbd.github.io/BeadInventory/models.json`。
设置页「AI 提供商」下面能选的模型，就来自这份清单。

- 拉到了，而且跟手机上的不同：换上新清单，并存一份在本地。JSON 里没写的 provider，保留手机上已有的那份。
- 拉不到（没网、Pages 挂了、JSON 写坏了）：用上次存下的清单；从来没拉到过就用代码里写死的内置清单（`ModelCatalogManager.builtIn`）。

## 格式

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "providers": {
    "Kimi": { "models": ["kimi-k2.6", "kimi-k3"], "default": "kimi-k2.6" }
  }
}
```

- `v` 必须是 1，否则整份不认。
- `providers` 的 key 必须跟 App 里的 provider 名字一字不差：`Kimi`、`OpenAI`、`Anthropic`、`Qwen`、`Gemini`。
- 某个 provider 不写，或者 `models` 是空的：那个 provider 保留手机上已有的清单。
- `models` 的顺序就是设置页里的显示顺序。
- `default` 必须在 `models` 里。写错了 App 会用 `models` 的第一个。`models` 和 `default` 两个字段都不能省略，任何一家少了字段或类型不对，整份清单都不认。
- 不认识的 provider key 会被忽略。以后加了新 provider，老版本 App 读到也不会出错（前提是新 provider 也带齐 `models` 和 `default`）。

## 用户的选择什么时候会被改

- 用户选的模型还在新清单里：**不动**。`default` 改成别的也不会覆盖用户的选择。
- 用户选的模型不在新清单里了（下线、改名）：换成新清单里这个 provider 的 `default`。
- 用户切换 provider 时，选中的是新清单里那个 provider 的 `default`。

所以下线一个模型，直接从 `models` 里删掉就行。

**只删官方已经下线的型号。** 官方还在提供服务的旧型号要留着，哪怕总览页上已经不列了。删掉的话，选着它的用户会被换到默认模型。判断有没有下线，看各家的弃用/下线公告和该型号自己的说明页。
